method: collect severity=blocker findings, sort by file+line, re-open evidence at index % 2 == 0

results.claim: Issue intake template 'Checks' item ('none of the items in "What you leave out"') tells filing agents to strip paths, file contents, logs, transcripts and prompts, contradicting the owner decision that AI-agent issue intake must send maximum debug data.
results.proof: docs/v2/review/agent-issue-intake/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml:11 reads verbatim 'Do not send settings, .env or MCP config files, logs, transcripts, file contents, paths, tokens or the user's own prompts.', and line 74 makes checking that list a required box, so the template as written blocks the maximum-debug-data rule the owner stated.

results.claim: Change #2's 'allow when the body does not reach stdout' rule drops v1's silent-flag and verbose-flag conditions for issue #166, so 'curl -o f url' and 'curl -s --verbose -o f url' would now be allowed, re-breaking the #166 stderr-flood fix.
results.proof: v1 cm-main hooks/core/routing.mjs:745-765 gates file-output curl/wget on both a verbose/trace check and a silent-flag check before calling it safe, and tests/hooks/core-routing.test.ts:178 and :186 assert both the no-silent and the '--verbose' cases are blocked; ADR-0008 r3's GP3 golden table (docs/v2/adr/0008-enforcement-rewrite-and-cap.md:55-66) has only one file-output row, 'curl -sL -o out.bin' -> allow, with no row for either dropped case, so the spec as written has no test forcing the silent/verbose checks to stay.

results.claim: Case B's PreToolUse 'allow' + updatedInput for a subagent Bash call rewrites the command to 'node <bundle>/run.mjs <base64>' before any deny/ask check runs, so the user's own Bash permission rules and other hooks never see the real command.
results.proof: ADR-0016 line 27 text matches the claim exactly: 'PreToolUse returns allow + updatedInput. The command becomes node <bundle>/run.mjs <base64 of the original>.' Nothing in that line, or in the surrounding 'Three cases' section (lines ~24-32), states that the original command is checked against deny/ask policy before the rewrite is issued, so a command that should be denied or need confirmation is allowed and rewritten unseen.

results.claim: P1299 'hooks: route quoted curl/wget stdout destinations' is marked as needing a v2 contract test, but no ADR or TECH-SPEC section names a quoted-argument parsing rule for the curl/wget interceptor.
results.proof: docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md:267 lists '#1299: quoted curl/wget destinations -> GP3' directly under the quoted-argument rule, and TECH-SPEC.md:289's GP3 row names 'PowerShell and quoted curl/wget routed' as a stated pass condition alongside issue #1299, so the contract test already has a named spec row to assert against; the finding's premise (no ADR/TECH-SPEC section names the rule) is false.
